accepted.question_text: Let H be a pr-graph, meaning a br-graph that is switching-equivalent to a graph with no pure blue edges. Let B_H := B x H be its bipartite resolution, where B is the purple K_2, so B_H has the parity-flip automorphism (i, v) -> (1 - i, v). A bipartite-min ordering of B_H is an ordering on each partite set that satisfies the underbar property, and it is special if every vertex has all neighbors joined by purple edges before its other neighbors. Is it true that B_H has a special bipartite-min ordering if and only if it has a special bipartite-min ordering that is parity-symmetric, i.e. commutes with the parity flip?

evidence.quote: A br-graph that is switching-equivalent to a graph with no pure blue edges is a pr-graph (for purple-red).

For a br-graph H, the bipartite resolution of H is BH := B x H. It is a bipartite br-graph with partite sets pi_B^-1(0) and pi_B^-1(1), so we call i = pi_B((i, v)) the parity of a vertex (i, v) and call the map f_p : (i, v) -> (1 - i, v), which is clearly an automorphism of BH, the parity flip map. A polymorphism phi of BH is parity-symmetric if it commutes with the parity flip map.
An ordering of the vertices of a bipartite graph H with partite sets U and V is a bipartite-min ordering if for any a, b in U and a', b' in V, the underbar property (2) holds.

Given a pr-graph H with a (bipartite-)min ordering of the underlying graph, a vertex is special if all its neighbours via purple edges come before its other neighbours. The ordering is a special (bipartite-)min ordering if all vertices are special.
Conjecture 1.4. For a pr-graph H, BH has a special bipartite-min ordering if and only if it has a parity-symmetric one.

accepted.question_text: For a br-graph H, let S_H be its switching graph. A k-ary weak near unanimity polymorphism is an idempotent polymorphism phi, for k >= 3, such that phi(x, x, ..., x, y) = phi(x, x, ..., y, x) = ... = phi(y, x, ..., x, x), and it is conservative when phi(v_1, ..., v_k) is always one of the inputs. Calling a polymorphism of S_H semi-conservative when it preserves symmetric lists, is it true that S_H has a semi-conservative weak near unanimity polymorphism if and only if S_H has a conservative weak near unanimity polymorphism?

evidence.quote: Let H be a br-graph, and S be the set {0, 1}. The switching graph SH of H is the br-graph on the set V(H) x S.

An idempotent polymorphism phi : H^k -> H, for k >= 3 is weak near unanimity or WNU if for every choice of x, y in V(H) we have phi(x, x, . . . , x, y) = phi(x, x, . . . , y, x) = . . . phi(y, x, . . . , x, x).
It is conservative if phi(v1, . . . , vk) in {v1, . . . , vk}.
Calling a polymorphism of SH semi-conservative if it conserves symmetric lists.
Question 6.1. Is it true for a br-graph H that (ii) SH has a semi-conservative WNU-polymorphism if and only if it has a conservative WNU-polymorphism?

accepted.question_text: For a br-graph H, let S_H be its switching graph. A 3-NU polymorphism phi : H^3 -> H satisfies phi(x, x, y) = phi(x, y, x) = phi(y, x, x) = x, and a polymorphism of S_H is called semi-conservative when it preserves symmetric lists. Is it true that S_H has a semi-conservative weak near unanimity polymorphism if and only if it has a semi-conservative 3-NU polymorphism?

evidence.quote: Let H be a br-graph, and S be the set {0, 1}. The switching graph SH of H is the br-graph on the set V(H) x S.

A polymorphism phi : H^3 -> H on a graph H is 3-NU if for any x, y in V(H), we have phi(x, x, y) = phi(x, y, x) = phi(y, x, x) = x.
Question 6.1. Is it true for a br-graph H that (iii) SH has a semi-conservative WNU-polymorphism if and only if it has a semi-conservative 3-NU-polymorphism?
